name: alarm_pipeline_cancel

path.note: the fully qualified Alarm Notification Pipeline path the Gateway reports (project:<name>:/pipeline:<name>); matched exactly, and a '*' is refused because the allowlist's wildcard is not a path

alarmEventId.note: the Alarm Event whose pipeline run is cancelled; the Gateway's own identifier, so the bound is deliberately looser than a UUID's 36 characters

preconditionToken.policy: D30 §2 lists no Precondition token for this Tool. Its concurrency rule is the pre-dispatch read and the bounded verification below: the run the caller addresses must exist at dispatch time, and an ambiguous dispatch whose run disappeared is never credited to this caller.

preDispatchRead.rule: D30 §2 attribution: a cancel's post-state is absence, which on its own proves nothing, so the Tool establishes the pre-state with the same bounded alarm_pipeline_status read it verifies with. A read that covers every run the Gateway matched and does not name the requested alarm event is `not_found`, and nothing is dispatched.

targetId.form: the exact Alarm Notification Pipeline path, as alarm_pipeline_list reports it
targetId.matchNote: D30 §6: exact pipeline paths or `*`, never prefixes. The Target is the caller's own path string, so an allowlist entry authorizes exactly the pipeline the Gateway reported for it and a path under (or above) it is a different Target.
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

fixedKnobsNote: D30 §4's fixed knobs govern config-resource writes, a Tag import's collision policy and a Project import's overwrite flag. This Tool sends exactly the two facts the documented route takes — path and alarmEventId — and nothing else, so it has no knob to fix.

inputBounds.path: 512 characters, refused with the requested length and the limit (D10)
inputBounds.alarmEventId: 128 characters, refused with the requested length and the limit (D10)
inputBounds.controlCharacters: refused in either input, so neither reaches an audit row or a log line
inputBounds.emptyComponents: invalid_argument, and a `*` in the path is invalid_argument rather than a Target lookup

readBound.source: alarm_pipeline_status, the read Tool D12 names as the canonical bounded verification source
readBound.page: one page at offset 0, at most 100 instances per call (D10)
readBound.exhaustiveWhen: the page covers every run the Gateway matched (matching - offset <= returned items)
readBound.unestablishedDisposition: limit_exceeded, naming the matched run count and the 100-instance bound; nothing is dispatched, and no partial read is ever treated as evidence

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is final for this Tool — a 4xx, or the 2xx the route documents carrying `success=false` with a problem. A cancelled run is not the caller's to claim when the Gateway refused the cancel, so the refusal is mapped to `conflict` (D30 §7: the run is no longer in the state the caller read) and no read-back may turn it into a success.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (a 2xx answering `success: true`) and the bounded re-read of the same pipeline path no longer reports a run for the requested alarm event
rejectionPolicy.uninterpretableResponse: a 2xx body this Tool cannot read as a claim (no `success` field, or the wrong type) is not a success either: the bounded re-read decides, and a change it cannot attribute to this call is outcome_unknown
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: an ambiguous dispatch (possibly sent with no response, or a 5xx) is reconciled only by the bounded re-read: a run still reported is `not_applied`, and a run that is gone is `outcome_unknown` — another operator may have cancelled the same run, so absence cannot be attributed to this call

verification: a bounded alarm_pipeline_status re-read of the same pipeline path, returned as Observed state: the instances that read served, and whether a run for the requested alarm event is still among them. A claimed success is confirmed only by that run being absent from a read that covered every match.
alarmEventUntouched: D12: cancelling a notification pipeline does not clear or acknowledge the Alarm Event. The Tool touches only the pipeline runtime route; it never calls an Alarm Event, Tag or configuration route.
